subject: Pricing & SLA — pay-as-you-grow cushion for AlphaTech pilot
messages:
From: Emma Carter <emma@alphatech.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@alphatech.io
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo questions — SLA bands and flexible commit option

Hi Soojin / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the latency numbers look promising for our inference-heavy workflows. Before we loop procurement in, two quick pricing/SLA questions so we can scope internally: 

1) Do you have a standard uptime/response banding (e.g., 99.5 / 99.9 / 99.99) tied to pricing? We want to see the delta for our cost modeling.
2) AlphaTech is early-stage on usage ramp — is there a way to structure a small initial commit with a "pay-as-you-grow" cushion (temporary overage credit or ramping commit) so we don't over-commit first quarter?

I attached an early SOW draft from our side (AlphaTech_SOW_draft_v2.pdf). If you have an SLA/pricing table, please share and we can pick a band to pilot.

If easier, we can jump on a 30-min call today.

Best,
Emma
Emma Carter
Head of ML Platforms
AlphaTech, Inc.
emma@alphatech.io
+1 (415) 555-0172

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Emma Carter <emma@alphatech.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo questions — SLA bands and flexible commit option

Hi Emma — great to meet today, thanks for the thoughtful questions. I've attached our SLA/pricing grid (sla_pricing_table.xlsx) and sketched two paths you can take — a conservative commit and a flexible pilot with a "pay-as-you-grow" cushion. High level:

- Bronze (cost-optimized): 99.5% uptime, 8 business-hour response for Sev 1, no guaranteed on-call. Lower unit price.
- Silver (balanced): 99.9% uptime, 4 hour response for Sev 1, 24/7 on-call in-scope for escalation; recommended for pilots with moderate traffic.
- Gold (enterprise): 99.99% uptime, 1 hour response Sev 1, prioritized routing and on-demand dedicated capacity options.

Pay-as-you-grow cushion (pilot model) — options we can offer:
- 90-day ramp credit: for the first 90d, we apply an overage credit equal to X% of overage tokens beyond the committed monthly volume (we typically model X between 40-60% depending on commitment).
- Step-commit ramp: commit at a lower baseline for Q1 with guaranteed step-up months and blended pricing for the first 6 months.
- Usage collar: short-term 20% buffer where we charge at a discounted overage rate to give you breathing room while you stabilize traffic patterns.

Example suggestion for AlphaTech pilot: start on Silver with a 90-day ramp credit (40% cushion) and a 6-month step-commit plan to convert to a modest annual commit if usage stabilizes. That gives you better support while not forcing a large upfront spend.

Next steps I propose:
1) If Silver sounds reasonable, we send a one-page pilot MPA + 90-day cushion language for procurement review.
2) Karthik and Jonas will draft a pricing anchor and I can share a mutual action plan (MVP milestones, expected volume ramp, success criteria).

Availability: I can jump on a call at 11:00 or 15:00 PT today.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com
(650) 555-0220

Attachment: sla_pricing_table.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Emma Carter <emma@alphatech.io>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo questions — SLA bands and flexible commit option

Emma / Soojin — quick note from pricing ops: happy to support the pay-as-you-grow approach for a pilot. A couple of guardrails and options so procurement has concrete numbers: 

- Discount mechanics: we can tier discounts against committed spend. Example: 0-50k/mo -> list price, 50-200k/mo -> 8% discount, 200k+ -> 15% discount (annualized commits). For pilots we often offer an additional 5% pilot discount applied to the first 3 invoice cycles.
- Cushion math: for the 90-day ramp credit, we recommend capping the credit to 1.5x the baseline monthly commit to avoid unbounded exposure. Example: baseline 100k tokens/month -> cushion covers overage up to 150k. Credits reconcile on the monthly invoice.
- SLA crediting: standard uptime SLA credits are defined in the SLA table (attached). For the pilot, we can add a limited remediation credit if an uptime breach occurs in the first 90 days — e.g., 25% service credit for a qualifying breach (one-time, pilot-only).

We should also clarify what counts as "severe" (Sev 1) vs operational issues — I'll include standard definitions in the MPA. Jonas can handle the operations handoff and confirm on-call cadence if AlphaTech goes Silver.

If this works, I'll turn the cushion and tier numbers into a short term sheet and MPA language today.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Pricing & Commercial Ops
karthik@redwood.com

From: Emma Carter <emma@alphatech.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@alphatech.io, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo questions — SLA bands and flexible commit option

Thanks — this is helpful and gives procurement the numbers they need. I reviewed the Silver recommendation and the cushion approach; AlphaTech is open to a short pilot with the following asks before we sign: 

- Pilot: Silver band, baseline commit 100k tokens/month, 90-day ramp credit covering overage up to 150k tokens/month at a 40% credit rate.
- SLA breach protection: if a qualifying uptime breach occurs in the first 90 days, we request a one-time remediation credit equal to 25% of that month’s invoice (as you proposed).
- MPA/DocuSign: please send the short MPA + DocuSign link and the mutual action plan (milestones and who owns the onboarding steps). We need the MPA in procurement by EOD Thursday to make the July 31st pilot start.

We attached our SOW (see attachment). Once we have the short MPA and DocuSign link we can route for procurement review.

On the call — happy to do 15 minutes tomorrow if you want to run through the MPA language.

Best,
Emma
Head of ML Platforms
AlphaTech, Inc.
